model.rationale: This southwestern Indiana seat leans heavily Republican, and first-term incumbent Mark Messmer holds a roughly four-to-one fundraising advantage over Democrat Mary Allen with no outside spending on either side. Prediction markets give Democrats only about a 3% chance, consistent with the district's fundamentals.
model.watch: Any emergence of polling showing a competitive race, or significant outside spending against Messmer, would be the first sign this is moving off safe Republican footing.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Indiana's 8th District is a strongly Republican seat in the state's southwestern corner, with a partisan lean of about 18 points toward the GOP. First-term Republican Mark Messmer is seeking reelection after clearing his primary, and he has raised roughly $1.2 million with about $714,000 on hand. Democrat Mary Allen has raised about $295,000, leaving her at a substantial financial disadvantage in a district that rarely sees competitive general elections.

No public general-election polling or expert race ratings are available for this contest, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbency advantage, and the money gap. Prediction markets currently price Democratic chances at only around 3%. Barring an unexpected development, Messmer is strongly favored to hold the seat.
